name: Zvartnots International Airport
before:
Armenia's main way in sits 15 km west of Yerevan and handles more traffic than anywhere else in the country. The runway takes everything up to an A380, and the main approach carries an ILS CAT II, which matters in winter because it allows landings down to a thirty metre ceiling.

Security runs in three stages on the way to the gates: a pre-control, passport control, then X-ray. Clients should be told to allow for it. Once through there is an Avolta duty free, the Converse Bank business class lounge looking out over the apron, a post office, a pharmacy and a spread of cafes and places to eat. Car hire is available from Europcar, and there are cash machines from the Armenian banks as well as HSBC and VTB.

Recent work has gone into the systems rather than the shell: a new flight information display, biometric bag drop and passenger checks, and 150 cameras across the site.
after:
Armenia's main international airport, about 12 km west of central Yerevan. The runway has a Category II landing system, which allows landings with cloud as low as 30 metres.

There is an Avolta duty free and a business lounge. Car hire firms have desks in the arrivals hall, and several banks have cash machines.

Zvartnots International Airport of Yerevan, is the main air gate of the Republic of Armenia

claims.claim: about 12 km west of central Yerevan
claims.inAfter: about 12 km west of central Yerevan
claims.note: Was 15 km. Wikipedia gives both 15 km and, for the drive, 12 km; coordinates give 10.3 km in a straight line at 252 degrees (west), so 15 km is a ratio of 1.46 and 12 km of 1.17. The road figure is used.

sources.quote: By car, the distance from Zvartnots Airport to the centre of Yerevan is 12 kilometers

quote: Straight-line distance from the city centre: 10.3 km (6.4 miles)
Bearing from the city centre: 252 degrees, which is west

claims.claim: Category II landing system, landings with cloud as low as 30 metres
claims.inAfter: The runway has a Category II landing system, which allows landings with cloud as low as 30 metres.
claims.note: The operator gives the minima as 30 m by 350 m; Wikipedia says 30 m and 300 m visibility. Only the 30 m ceiling, on which they agree, is stated.

sources.quote: Runway 08 is equipped with an ILS CAT II, which enables aircraft operations in low ceiling (30 meters)
The navigation system installed on the runway ensures 30x350m meteorological minimum for landing, which corresponds to the ICAO 2nd class.

claims.inAfter: There is an Avolta duty free

The operator also says it is open 24 hours and takes Priority Pass and LoungeKey (25,000 AMD online otherwise), but that has one source, so it is not stated.
